teaching_language: Fully English-taught (case 1). The entire 2-year, 120-ECTS second-cycle degree is delivered in English ('An innovative post-graduate Master Programme in advanced European, international and transnational legal studies entirely in English'). It is a single UNITO degree, NOT an English pathway inside an Italian-named programme and NOT an interuniversity/joint degree. Two clarifications: (a) the degree is jointly governed by two UNITO departments - Department of Law (lead) and the Department of Economics and Statistics 'Cognetti de Martiis' - but both are within the University of Turin, so it is not an interuniversity degree; (b) an OPTIONAL double-degree track exists with the Faculty of Law of Universite Savoie Mont Blanc (Chambery, France), where students may spend the second year abroad with an integrated curriculum (max 5 UNITO students, selected via the Erasmus Mobility Call for Studies) - this is an elective mobility option for already-enrolled students, not the default structure of the degree. UNITO explicitly warns that ELS is NOT an LLM programme: it is an Italian Laurea magistrale. No Italian-language teaching component is required for admission.
campus: Turin (Torino), Piedmont, Italy. Teaching seat: Turin - Campus Luigi Einaudi (Lungo Dora Siena 100/A); admission interviews for national applicants have historically been held in the Meeting Room, block D2, 2nd floor, Campus Einaudi (recent cycles have moved the interview online). Governing departments: Department of Law (Dipartimento di Giurisprudenza) and Department of Economics and Statistics 'Cognetti de Martiis'; organising structure: School of Law, Political and Economic-Social Sciences. Programme office contact: info.els@unito.it, tel. +39 011 670 9409/9410.
degree_class: LM-90 (Studi europei / European Studies) for Cohort 2024 and previous cohorts; LM-90R (the reformed 'R' class) from Cohort 2025 onward. UNITO internal programme code from Cohort 2025: 0703M22. Type of course: Second Cycle Degree (Laurea magistrale), 2 years, 120 ECTS, teaching mode 'conventional'. [uncertain]
admission_type: Open access / no restricted number of places (corso senza numero programmato) BUT with a mandatory eligibility check: admission is subject to (1) verification of specific academic curricular requirements (minimum ECTS in named subject areas) and (2) a compulsory admission interview in English before an ELS Admissions Commission that evaluates the candidate's profile, preparation, motivation and English proficiency. It is therefore 'open access with selective profile assessment' rather than a numerus clausus with ranked selection. No TOLC, SAT or written entrance exam is used. Reserved quotas do exist even though the programme is open access: 50 places reserved for non-EU citizens residing abroad and 5 places reserved for Marco Polo programme students. Two separate application channels apply: applicants holding an ITALIAN qualification apply via MyUniTo ('Pre-iscrizione ai corsi ad accesso libero') and book an interview slot; applicants holding a FOREIGN (non-Italian) qualification, and all international students, must apply through the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it, course id 342), where the Commission evaluates the CV plus motivation letter and then holds a video interview.
application_deadline_eu: For a.y. 2026/2027, applicants with a FOREIGN qualification who are Italians, EU citizens, EU-equivalents or non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy apply through Apply@UniTo. The relevant window is the Fourth admission call, reserved to open access postgraduate degree programmes: 25 August - 8 September 2026, with the course page showing the hard deadline as 8 September 2026, 23:59:59 Central European Time. This group could alternatively have used the First admission call (25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026), which was open to all applicants for postgraduate degree programmes. Applicants holding an ITALIAN qualification do not use Apply@UniTo: they book an admission interview on MyUniTo within the application windows published each year on the programme's 'How to apply' page (in past cycles three windows running roughly late June to late November, each closing at 12 noon a few days before the interview date); the specific 2026/2027 windows and interview dates could not be recovered because the programme microsite is unreachable. A non-refundable EUR 60 application fee must be paid within the deadline of each Apply@UniTo call (the fee is the same whether you apply for one or two programmes). [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: For a.y. 2026/2027, non-EU citizens residing abroad (visa applicants) could only use the First admission call: 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026, which was the single Apply@UniTo window 'open to all applicants wishing to apply for postgraduate degree programs'. All later 2026/2027 calls (third, fourth and fifth) are explicitly reserved to Italians, EU and EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy - the fourth call currently shown on the ELS course page carries the notice 'This call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy. If you apply without this prerequisite, your application will not be considered.' Successful non-EU applicants must additionally submit the pre-enrolment (visa) application on the Universitaly platform by the ministerial deadline (mid-July 2026 for a.y. 2026/2027) and complete visa formalities at the competent Italian diplomatic mission. As of the research date (1 September 2026) the non-EU-abroad window for 2026/2027 is closed; the equivalent 2027/2028 first call would be expected around late November 2027 - late January 2028 but is not yet published. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: No standardised admission test (no TOLC, no GRE/GMAT, no SAT) and no written entrance examination. The selection instrument is a COMPULSORY ADMISSION INTERVIEW held in English by the ELS Admissions Commission (composed of Law Department faculty members; in recent cycles Professors Oddenino, Montaldo and Mola). Purpose of the interview: to verify the adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation, motivation, compliance with the enrolment requirements, and English language proficiency (which must be at least CEFR B2). Format: applicants with an Italian qualification book a slot via MyUniTo and attend on one of a small number of published dates (historically in person at Campus Einaudi, with an online option on request for applicants meeting UNITO's stated conditions; recent cycles have been held online). International applicants applying through Apply@UniTo are assessed on their CV and motivation letter and then invited to a VIDEO INTERVIEW. The Commission may assign an 'integration of the programme' or additional preparation as a condition for admission, and a candidate who does not yet hold the required ECTS may sit the interview but can only enrol after evidencing the missing credits.
academic_requirements: 1) QUALIFICATION: a first-cycle degree (Bachelor's / Italian Laurea Triennale) obtained after at least 3 years of university education. Candidates must already have graduated in order to enrol; a not-yet-graduated candidate may book an interview but cannot enrol until the degree certificate is submitted (at least 5 working days before the enrolment deadline). 2) CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS - a certified academic record (transcript) evidencing a minimum of: 15 ECTS/CFU in Private Law (also comparative), Constitutional/Public Law or Comparative Law (Italian SSD codes IUS/01, IUS/02, IUS/08, IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/21); 15 ECTS/CFU in International Law and European Union Law (SSD IUS/13, IUS/14); and 6 ECTS/CFU in Economics (SSD SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/07). For applicants with an ITALIAN qualification, holding an L-14 class degree (Scienze dei servizi giuridici) or an L-16 class degree (Scienze dell'Amministrazione e dell'Organizzazione) is an alternative route that satisfies the curricular requirement automatically. 3) FLEXIBILITY MARGIN: the admission Committee may grant a margin of flexibility of up to 10% of the ECTS credits required in each sector, where the student's profile demonstrates appropriate knowledge and expertise in the relevant areas. 4) GRADE THRESHOLDS (evaluation criteria, not automatic bars): particular importance is given to the first-cycle graduation grade - a grade below 98/110 on the Italian scale, or the proportional equivalent in a foreign grading system, is stated to be 'a key negative evaluation criterion'; in addition, for international applicants, a first-cycle final AVERAGE grade below 80% of the maximum available in the candidate's own university grading system is likewise a key negative evaluation criterion. 5) PERSONAL PREPARATION is assessed by the Commission through the CV, the motivation letter, the graduation/average grade and the admission interview; the Commission reserves the power to assign additional preparation to obtain a positive evaluation. 6) PLACES: no restricted number of places overall; 50 places reserved for non-EU citizens residing abroad and 5 places reserved for Marco Polo students. 7) Foreign qualifications must be recognised as giving access to second-cycle study, and UNITO's International Students Office may require a Declaration of Value or a CIMEA Statement of Verification / Statement of Comparability after submission.
language_requirements: ENGLISH: CEFR B2 (upper intermediate) is the minimum entry level. It must be CERTIFIED - 'English language skills shall be equivalent to the B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR - upper intermediate) and shall be certified' - and it is ALSO tested directly by the Admissions Commission during the admission interview ('The Committee will verify in the admission interview the candidates' English language proficiency, that shall be equivalent to at least a B2 level'). For applicants with an Italian qualification, UNITO accepts a language certification OR a self-certification ('language certification/self-certification'), with details published on the programme's 'How to Apply' page; for international applicants via Apply@UniTo, an English language certificate is listed among the additional documents that may be required under the 'Language requirements' section of the course description. No specific minimum IELTS/TOEFL band, and no explicit list of accepted certificates or exemption rules (e.g. for graduates of English-medium bachelor's degrees or native speakers), could be confirmed on an accessible official page. ITALIAN: no Italian language requirement and no Italian certificate is needed for admission, because the programme is taught entirely in English; UNITO's rule requiring a B2 Italian certificate for non-EU visa applicants applies only to Italian-taught programmes. Italian courses are offered to enrolled students as a support service ('Learning Italian'), not as an entry condition. [uncertain]
required_documents: A) APPLICANTS WITH AN ITALIAN QUALIFICATION (MyUniTo 'Pre-iscrizione ai corsi ad accesso libero'): 1) transcript of records / academic record with the degree or enrolment certificate; 2) English language certification or self-certification; 3) Curriculum Vitae; 4) identity document. If credits or the degree are still missing at interview time, the relevant certificate must be sent to corsistudio.giurisprudenza.cle@unito.it at least 5 working days before the enrolment deadline. B) APPLICANTS WITH A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION / INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS (Apply@UniTo, apply.unito.it course 342): 1) valid passport or identity document; 2) first-cycle degree certificate (Bachelor's diploma) obtained after at least 3 years of university study; 3) official transcript of records evidencing the required minimum ECTS in Private/Public/Comparative Law, International and EU Law, and Economics; 4) MOTIVATION LETTER in English or Italian (explicitly listed as mandatory under 'Other requirements' for this programme); 5) Curriculum Vitae; 6) English language certification at CEFR B2 or above; 7) optional but recommended: the degree programme syllabus / course description issued by the foreign institution, with translation; 8) certified translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish of any document not issued in one of those four languages (entry qualification documents are accepted as they are in English, French, Italian or Spanish); 9) payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the call deadline. After submission UNITO may request further documents (Declaration of Value, CIMEA Statement of Verification or Statement of Comparability), and the International Students Office may request additional documentation again at the enrolment step. Incomplete applications are rejected.

uncertainty_notes:
SOURCE ACCESS SITUATION: mixed, and better than for most UNITO programmes in this batch.
- apply.unito.it WAS reachable directly when fetched with a standard desktop browser User-Agent via curl (HTTP 200). The Apply@UniTo course page for European Legal Studies (course id 342), the 2026/2027 call calendar page and the required-documentation page were all read first-hand and in full on 1 September 2026. These are the strongest sources here and cover entry qualification, curricular ECTS requirements, evaluation criteria, English requirement, motivation letter, non-EU quota, fees, application fee and the 2026/27 deadline. WebFetch itself still returned HTTP 403 for the same URLs (Cloudflare), so the UA workaround was essential.
- www.europeanlegalstudies.unito.it (the programme's own microsite, i.e. official_program_url) was completely unreachable: TLS connections were refused at network level (ECONNREFUSED 130.186.3.24:443) for both WebFetch and curl, with and without a browser User-Agent. Its content was recovered from (a) Wayback Machine snapshots - admission-requirements.html captured 2024-11-09 (page last updated 2024-06-05, covering a.y. 2024/2025) and how_to_enroll.html captured 2024-04-18 (page last updated 2023-06-13, covering a.y. 2023/2024) - and (b) search-engine indexed extracts of the current live pages.
- en.unito.it returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to every attempt including the browser-UA curl; its content (degree record 86719, scholarships, tuition pages) is reflected only through indexed search extracts.

SPECIFIC OPEN POINTS:
1) DEGREE CLASS TRANSITION: the archived 2024 microsite states 'Second Cycle Degree LM-90'; a current indexed extract of the same key_information page states 'LM-90R (from Cohort 2025)' with programme code 0703M22, and that LM-90 applies to Cohort 2024 and previous. This is consistent with the Italian ministerial reform introducing 'R' classes, but the LM-90R designation and the 0703M22 code come from a search extract rather than a first-hand page read, so degree_class is marked uncertain.
2) MARCO POLO QUOTA: the '5 places reserved for Marco Polo students' figure comes from indexed extracts of the key_information page. The Apply@UniTo page independently confirms only the 50 non-EU-residing-abroad places. The Marco Polo number is therefore less firmly established.
3) NATIONAL-APPLICANT INTERVIEW DATES FOR 2026/2027 ARE NOT KNOWN. The only interview calendar recovered is the 2023/2024 one (application windows 26 Jun - 4 Sep 2023, 18 Sep - 9 Oct 2023, 23 Oct - 20 Nov 2023, with interviews on 13 Sep, 18 Oct and 29 Nov 2023). The structure (three windows, MyUniTo booking, closing at 12 noon) is very likely unchanged, but the actual 2026/2027 dates must be checked on the live 'How to apply' page. application_deadline_eu is marked uncertain for this reason.
4) NON-EU DEADLINE IS INFERRED FROM THE UNIVERSITY-WIDE CALENDAR, not from a programme-specific statement. The Apply@UniTo calendar shows the First admission call (25 Nov 2025 - 29 Jan 2026) as the only 2026/2027 window open to all applicants for postgraduate programmes, and calls three to five are explicitly restricted to EU/EU-equivalent/Italy-resident applicants. It was not independently confirmed that European Legal Studies specifically participated in the first call, nor was the exact Universitaly pre-enrolment (visa) deadline for 2026/2027 verified on an accessible official page - the mid-July date is carried over from UNITO's standard practice.
5) ENGLISH CERTIFICATE DETAIL: the requirement is clearly CEFR B2, certified, plus interview verification. However, no accessible official page lists which certificates are accepted, the minimum IELTS/TOEFL scores, or whether graduates of English-medium bachelor's degrees or native speakers are exempt. The archived microsite indicates that applicants with Italian qualifications may use a SELF-certification, which suggests the requirement is applied flexibly, but this is a 2023/2024-era statement.
6) ADMISSION-TYPE NUANCE: the programme is formally 'open access' (no numerus clausus), yet enrolment is genuinely conditional on passing an interview and meeting quantified ECTS thresholds, and reserved international quotas exist. It should not be presented to applicants as unconditional open access.
7) GRADE CRITERIA ARE 'KEY NEGATIVE EVALUATION CRITERIA', NOT HARD CUT-OFFS. Both the 98/110 graduation-grade threshold and the 80%-of-maximum average-grade threshold are described as strongly negative factors in the Commission's assessment; the sources do not state that a candidate below them is automatically rejected.
8) TWO NUMERICALLY DIFFERENT GRADE RULES coexist (98/110 graduation grade; 80% average grade). The apply.unito.it page lists both; the archived microsite listed only the 98/110 rule. Applicants should assume both apply for the 2026/27 international channel.
9) FEES: the EUR 156 - EUR 2,800 range is officially quoted for a.y. 2025-26. For 2026-27 UNITO has moved international students to a scale based on GDP per capita (PPP) of the country of residence; no programme-specific 2026-27 figure was verifiable, and there is no ELS-specific fee page.
10) COHORT/CODE HISTORY: en.unito.it exposes at least three different degree record ids for this programme (86719, 63239, 45593), corresponding to different cohorts of the same degree. This is a UNITO catalogue artefact, not three different programmes.
11) DOUBLE DEGREE: the Turin-Chambery double degree is an optional second-year mobility track selected through the Erasmus Mobility Call for Studies (max 5 UNITO students), not part of the standard admission route; it does not make the base degree an interuniversity/joint programme.
12) Per task scope, no polito.it sources were used; all substantive content comes from unito.it origins (apply.unito.it live, europeanlegalstudies.unito.it via Wayback and indexed extracts, en.unito.it via indexed extracts).
